If we approximate and assume the question is asking about the change in kinetic energy:
W = KEf - KEi = 7.515 × 10^-23 J - 3.34 × 10^-21 J = -2.5885 × 10^-21 J. This is closest to -2.17 × 10^-21 J.

(b) We can estimate the strength of the force using the change in momentum. The change in momentum is equal to the force multiplied by the time interval over which the force acts, so Δp = F * Δt. Since we don't know the time interval, we can estimate it using the distance over which the collision occurred and the speed of the neutron.
Δx = 2 × 10^-5 m
Δv = 3 × 10^2 m/s - 2 × 10^3 m/s = -1900 m/s
Δt ≈ Δx / Δv = (2 × 10^-5 m) / (-1900 m/s) ≈ -1.053 × 10^-8 s
F = Δp / Δt = m * Δv / Δt = (1.67 × 10^-27 kg) * (-1900 m/s) / (-1.053 × 10^-8 s) ≈ 3.17 × 10^-6 N
